records.name: ILMUNC (Ivy League Model United Nations Conference)
records.notes: A nonprofit that runs one student Model UN conference a year in downtown Philadelphia (venue: Marriott Philadelphia Downtown; no street address on the site). The way in is registering as a delegate for one conference, which is an event rather than a standing group, so the verdict is not_a_group. Next event on the page: ILMUNC XLIII, January 21 to 24, 2027. The site mentions a student secretariat but describes no volunteer applications. The registration page was not read, so fees are unknown. The group also runs conferences abroad (Vietnam, India, China). A reviewer may prefer to publish annual conference programs instead.

records.name: My Brother's Keeper Cares
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that works on mental health and suicide prevention. It runs community events, mentoring, chess and golf programs, and art therapy.
records.what_you_do: Come to the community mental health events, take part in the chess and golf programs, or join the mailing list and volunteer through the group's website.

schedule.text: Events are posted on the website as they are planned. No regular weekly meeting time is listed.

cost.text: No cost listed on the site

first_step.how: Visit the volunteer page at MBKCares.com or join the mailing list to hear about the next event
first_step.basis: The site has a public volunteer page and a mailing list, and it does not mention a membership requirement.

records.notes: IRS legal name: My Brothers Keeper Cares Inc. The only date on the site is 'Checkmate & Clubhouse Programs 2025', with no month, so status is probably_active and no last_sign_of_life is recorded. The site lists no phone or email; use its Contact Us page. Social accounts named on the site: Facebook (MBKCares), Instagram, Twitter and YouTube, each under the handle mbkcares. Mentorship and art therapy are listed under What We Do without times.

records.name: New Hope Philly
records.summary: A non-denominational Christian church in Southwest Philadelphia. It offers Sunday worship, separate men's and women's Bible studies, and help for people working through addiction.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship, join a men's or women's Bible study, or ask about the addiction support, counseling and GED or other classes offered through the church.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am. Men's Bible study on Tuesdays at 7 pm. Women's Bible study on the first and third Saturdays at 11 am.

cost.text: No cost listed; the site asks for donations

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 11 am at 5520 Woodland Ave, or call 267-201-2419 to ask about the Bible studies
first_step.basis: Services and Bible studies are listed publicly, with a phone number to ask about joining.

records.notes: IRS legal name: New Hope Philly Inc. The footer shows '@ 2013', which is not evidence of activity. The site has no dated events or news. The Bible studies are split by gender (men on Tuesdays, women on the first and third Saturdays). The site also asks for prayer and for donations toward a field next to the building, and lists an intern application. It describes addiction support and counseling as services, not as a support group, so support_group is false and no support-recovery tag was used. A reviewer may want to add one.

records.name: No More Dysphoria
records.summary: A trans and nonbinary-led organizing project in Philadelphia. It builds peer support and political education so the community can push back on state violence and keep access to care.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on the ground in Philadelphia, in person or remotely, or reach out to hear about current projects.

schedule.text: No meeting times are posted. The group asks people to get in touch to volunteer.

first_step.how: Email nomoredysphoria@gmail.com and say you want to volunteer in Philadelphia, in person or remotely
first_step.basis: The site invites new volunteers to reach out, with no application or membership listed.

records.notes: The site gives its address as Montclair, NJ, and asks for volunteers on the ground in Philadelphia. The IRS record lists a South Philadelphia address (1218 S Saint Bernard St) that the site does not show. The site has no dated events or news. Instagram and X accounts use the handle @nomoredysphoria. Donations go through PayPal. No program names are listed. No tag exists for trans and nonbinary rights, so womens_lgbtq_rights is the closest fit.

records.name: Ordinarie Heroes
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps young people build leadership, school and career skills. It also runs a mobile pantry, an educational farm and nutrition workshops.
records.what_you_do: Young people take part in weekly in-person leadership sessions, tutoring, film and photo workshops, and college and career prep. Volunteers sign up through the site's Connect page.

schedule.text: Staff are in the office Monday to Friday, 2 to 8 pm, and on Saturdays for scheduled events. Leadership sessions run weekly in person.

first_step.how: Call (215) 385-5135 or email info@ohmovement.org to ask about the next leadership session, or use the Connect page to volunteer
first_step.basis: The site has a public sign-up form for young people and a Connect page for volunteers, with a phone and email to ask questions. It does not describe what a first session is like.

records.notes: Also called OH Movement on the site, where the IE in the name stands for I'm Enough. IRS legal name: Ordinarie Heroes. Mailing address 828 S Alden St, 19143 (not a meeting place). The site lists no dated events or news. The age range for participants is not stated on the site, so no crowd tags were set.

records.name: Pathfinder Strategic Services

records.name: PA ACE Women's Network
records.summary: A statewide network of women leaders in Pennsylvania higher education. Members get workshops, networking events and mentoring, including a STEM mentorship network.
records.what_you_do: Join as a member to take part in the workshops, networking events and mentoring. The Memberships page on paacenet.org explains how to join.

schedule.text: Events are listed on the website with a month and day but no year. Examples include a virtual workshop on restorative practices and an in-person networking event.

locations.label: Statewide across Pennsylvania, with virtual and in-person events

cost.text: Membership fees are not listed on the site

first_step.how: Check the Memberships page on paacenet.org for fees and what members get, then look at the listed events
first_step.basis: Joining is the main way in and the fees are not shown, so a visitor cannot see what it is like before paying.

records.notes: The IRS record lists 1 University Mews, 19104 and Holy Family University as the contact. The site shows no street address. Event dates on the site have no years, so the newest date cannot be confirmed and status is a working-site judgment. Social accounts on the site are Facebook, LinkedIn and Instagram (no URLs captured). Audience is set to members because joining is the main way in; the site does not say which events are members only.

records.name: Pennsylvania Sibling Support Network
records.notes: Per its current site, a nonprofit that provides waiver-funded in-home and companion services for people with intellectual disabilities. The site lists no support groups, events or volunteer roles, so there is no group to join today. Older search results (a 2015 to 2016 resource guide and siblingleadership.org) describe a monthly sibling support group and a statewide sibling program; neither appears on the current site. The batch website 'Pennsylvania Sibling Support' was a name, not an address; the one search led to www.passn.org, which redirects to pssn.org. Phone 215-240-9967 and email info@pssnonline.org are published on the site. Verdict not_a_group. A reviewer may prefer a re-check for a sibling support group.

records.name: Philadelphia Family Pride
records.summary: A membership group for LGBTQ+ families in the Philadelphia area. It hosts get-togethers and family events, runs resource fairs, and offers classes for people thinking about becoming parents.
records.what_you_do: Come to the informal get-togethers and family events, take a prospective parent class, or join as a member.

schedule.text: Events and informal get-togethers are posted on the website as they are planned.

first_step.how: Join as a member, or check the upcoming events on the site and come to one
first_step.basis: Public events and resource pages can be read without signing in, and joining is a clear button on the site. The page does not say which events need membership.

records.notes: Mailing address PO Box 31848, Philadelphia, PA 19104 (on the site). The site lists an email, but the text we read shows it obfuscated, so it is not recorded. Newest dated item: a November 2025 newsletter. Listed programs include a 2025 Resource Fair, the Family Matters Conference, prospective parent classes, foster parent recruitment and a Juneteenth picnic. Social accounts named: Facebook, Twitter, Instagram and YouTube (no URLs captured). The parent classes and foster recruitment are not tagged as playgroups, so parent_playgroups and foster_care_support are the closest fits.

notes: Verdicts: 6 publish with full records (My Brother's Keeper Cares, New Hope Philly, No More Dysphoria, Ordinarie Heroes, PA ACE Women's Network, Philadelphia Family Pride); 5 publish with status unknown and held back, with no summary, categories or interests (Institute of Jewish Spirituality and Society, Joan Samuels Foundation, Learning Station Academy CDC, Literacy and More Inc, New Beginning in Christ Deliverance Ministry); 1 out_of_area (ICIAM); 3 not_a_group (ILMUNC, Pathfinder Strategic Services, Pennsylvania Sibling Support Network). Searches: 2 of 2 used. One went to Pennsylvania Sibling Support Network (its batch field was a name, not an address; the search led to pssn.org). The other went to Learning Station Academy CDC (no page found). The budget ran out before Joan Samuels, the Institute of Jewish Spirituality and Society, Literacy and More and New Beginning could be searched, so those four stay unknown and need a second pass. Fetches: 21 of 60 used. Checked and dropped: Sibling Leadership Network (siblingleadership.org) is a national network with no Pennsylvania or Philadelphia chapter listed, so it is not a Philadelphia group. Batch fields that are not web addresses were treated as missing: 'Literacy and More Inc.', 'Pennsylvania Sibling Support', and the email address on New Beginning in Christ. Personal contact names from the IRS batch were not recorded. Joan Samuels and the Institute of Jewish Spirituality may be private foundations or nonprofits with no public way in; a reviewer should check before they go live.
